body:
Two changes to `json_pointer`. Instructions, macOS / Linux GCC 13 / Linux Clang 18:

| commit | change |
|---|---|
| Split a JSON pointer in one scan and construct the tokens in place | parsing citm 42.3 -> 36.4M / -18 % / -16 %; twitter -9 ... -12 % |
| Copy the tokens of a pointer without escapes straight into `to_string()` | citm 47.5 -> 30.6M / -23 % / -36 %; twitter -32 % / -18 % / -32 % |

`at()`, `contains()`, `unflatten()` and `patch()` are unchanged (+-0.2 %).

## Numbers

macOS timing vs develop: JsonPointerToString 0.71, JsonPointerParse 0.85.

## Validation

- Differential check against develop: random pointer strings for parse, `to_string()`, `back()`, `pop_back()`, `parent_pointer()`, `/`, `at()`, `contains()`, `value()` and `operator[]`. Exception ids and messages are identical.
- Unit tests with ASan/UBSan, in C++11 and C++20.
- All commits build on their own, and each commit's `single_include` is a fresh `make amalgamate`.

## Public API

No breaking changes.

Written by Claude Code on behalf of @nlohmann.

Should there be an early return for `length == 0`?

Right: an empty pointer now returns `string_t()` at the top of `to_string()`, before the scan loop, and the copy path no longer needs its `length != 0` guard. Fixed in `75e067e3d`.
